summary: This note is a Wikipedia-derived overview of Mali, a landlocked West African country, covering its demographics, history, government, languages, economy, health situation and ethnic relations. It traces key episodes including the Songhai Empire's collapse after a 1591 Moroccan invasion, the 1968 coup led by Moussa Traoré, the 1991 coup that followed protests, and the 2012–2013 northern conflict. It also notes the country's limited medical facilities and high rates of child malnutrition and female genital mutilation.
one_line: Overview of Mali, a landlocked West African country covering its population, history, government, languages, economy, health and ethnic tensions.
key_facts: In 2007, about 48 percent of Malians were younger than 12 years old and the median age was 15.9 years.
Life expectancy at birth in Mali was 53.06 years total, 51.43 for males and 54.73 for females.
Mali had 106 infant deaths per 1,000 live births in 2007, one of the world's highest infant mortality rates.
The Songhai Empire's eventual collapse was largely the result of a Moroccan invasion in 1591 under the command of Judar Pasha.
In January 2012 an armed conflict broke out in northern Mali, and Tuareg rebels declared the secession of a new state, Azawad.
In January 2013 the French military launched Opération Serval in response to Islamist territorial gains in northern Mali.
Presidential elections in Mali were held on 28 July 2013, with a second round run-off on 11 August 2013.
The unicameral National Assembly consists of deputies elected to five-year terms, and the Alliance for Democracy and Progress held 113 of 160 seats after the 2007 elections.
On 19 November 1968 the Keïta regime was overthrown in a bloodless military coup led by Moussa Traoré, now commemorated as Liberation Day.
On 26 March 1991, Lieutenant Colonel Amadou Toumani Touré announced on the radio that he had arrested the dictatorial president, Moussa Traoré.
Mali's official language is French, and about 80% of the population can communicate in Bambara, an important lingua franca.
Mali is the eighth-largest country in Africa, and its capital is Bamako.
Mali is the third largest producer of gold on the African continent, and its economy centers on agriculture and mining.
An estimated 85–91 percent of Mali's girls and women have had female genital mutilation, according to 2006 and 2001 data.
An estimated 1.9 percent of the adult and children population was afflicted with HIV/AIDS, among the lowest rates in Sub-Saharan Africa.
